name: date.add_interval
title: Add time
summary: Add an amount of seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (a month added to 31 January is 28 or 29 February).

name: date.subtract_interval
title: Subtract time
summary: Take away an amount of seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years.

name: date.from_timezone
title: Read as a time zone
summary: Say which time zone times without one were written in, so they become exact moments (a time that the clocks skipped, or passed twice, is empty).

name: date.to_utc
title: Convert to UTC
summary: Write moments in UTC. Times without a zone are read in the zone given (or as UTC already when none is).

name: date.is_holiday
title: Is a public holiday
summary: True on the public holidays of a country (and region), from each country's published rules.

name: date.holiday_name
title: Name of the public holiday
summary: The name of the public holiday on that day, or empty.

name: date.fiscal_period
title: Fiscal month
summary: Which month of the financial year (1 to 12), for a year starting in the month given.

name: date.spine
title: Make a calendar of dates
summary: Replace the rows with one row for every day (or week, month, quarter, year) from this column's earliest date to its latest, or between dates you give: a calendar to join other data to, with no day missing.

name: date.fill_missing
title: Add rows for missing dates
summary: Add a row for each date a series skipped, between its first and last date (within each group), with the other columns empty; optionally a column saying which rows were added.

name: assert.not_empty
title: Check nothing is empty
summary: Every row has a value in these columns.

name: assert.in_set
title: Check values are from a list
summary: Every value of the column is one of these (empty values pass; check them with Check nothing is empty).

name: assert.in_range
title: Check numbers are in a range
summary: Every value is a number at least the lowest and at most the highest given.

name: assert.matches
title: Check values match a pattern
summary: Every value matches a regular expression in full.

name: assert.type
title: Check values are of a type
summary: Every value reads as a number, a whole number, a date or true or false.

name: assert.formula
title: Check a formula holds
summary: Every row satisfies a formula that is true or false, such as [shipped] >= [ordered]; a row where it is empty fails.

name: assert.found_in
title: Check every key exists elsewhere
summary: Every value of the column appears in another dataset's column (each order's customer is a known customer): referential integrity.

name: assert.unique
title: Check values are unique
summary: No two rows have the same values in these columns (a key).

name: assert.no_duplicates
title: Check no row is repeated
summary: No two rows are the same in every column.

name: assert.row_count
title: Check the number of rows
summary: There are at least, or at most, this many rows (an import that brought nothing; a join that multiplied).

name: assert.increasing
title: Check values only go up
summary: Each value of the column is at least the one before it (or, strictly, more): a sequence, a running total, timestamps in order.

name: assert.sum_equals
title: Check a total
summary: The column adds up to this, within a tolerance (shares add to 100, debits equal credits).

name: assert.fresh
title: Check the data is recent
summary: The newest date or time in the column is no older than this many hours when the recipe runs (a replay checks against the moment of the run it repeats).

name: assert.schema
title: Check the columns
summary: The data has these columns (each optionally with a type, as name:number, name:date, name:text, name:true or false), and, if asked, no others.

name: assert.distribution_stable
title: Check values look as they did
summary: The column's values are distributed as in another dataset, such as this recipe's own output from the run before: by the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance for numbers and the population stability index for categories, below a threshold.

name: clean.email
title: Standardise an email
summary: Trim and lower case. Empty results become null.

name: clean.email_domain
title: Email domain
summary: The part after the @, lower case.

name: clean.phone
title: Standardise a phone number
summary: Best-effort E.164. Numbers that cannot be made sense of become null.

name: clean.url
title: Standardise a URL
summary: Add a scheme where one is missing.

name: clean.url_part
title: Part of a URL
summary: Pull out the scheme, host, path, query or fragment.

name: clean.postal_code
title: Standardise a postal code
summary: Apply the country's usual spacing and padding.

name: clean.country
title: Standardise a country
summary: Map country names and abbreviations to an ISO code. Unrecognised names become null.

name: clean.name_part
title: Split a full name
summary: Take the first, middle or last name. Particles stay with the surname.

name: clean.boolean_tokens
title: Standardise yes/no
summary: Read Y/N, yes/no, 1/0, on/off as true and false.

name: clean.line_endings
title: Standardise line endings
summary: Turn Windows and old-Mac line endings into plain newlines.

name: clean.control_characters
title: Remove control characters
summary: Strip the invisible characters that break exports.

name: clean.mojibake
title: Fix mangled characters
summary: Repair text where UTF-8 was read as Latin-1 -- the Â£ and â€™ problem.

name: clean.trim_quotes
title: Trim surrounding quotes
summary: Remove quote marks left by a bad export.

name: clean.unescape
title: Unescape
summary: Turn backslash escapes back into the characters they stand for.

name: clean.standardise
title: Tidy up text
summary: Collapse whitespace and apply a consistent case, in one step.

name: columns.move
title: Move columns
summary: Move columns to the start or the end, leaving the rest in order.

name: columns.sort
title: Sort columns by name
summary: Put the columns in alphabetical order.

name: columns.keep_only
title: Keep only these columns
summary: Drop everything else, in the dataset's own order.

name: columns.drop
title: Drop columns
summary: Remove one or more columns.

name: columns.duplicate
title: Duplicate a column
summary: Add a copy, so the original survives an experiment.

name: columns.rename
title: Rename a column
summary: Give a column a new name.

name: columns.bulk_rename
title: Rename many columns
summary: Apply one renaming rule to every column at once.

name: join.as_of
title: Join to the nearest earlier row
summary: Bring columns from the other dataset's row that comes just before (or after, or nearest) this row's date or number, optionally matching other columns first: the exchange rate in force on the day, the price at the time of the order.

name: join.range
title: Join where a value is in a range
summary: Bring columns from the other dataset's rows whose range (from a low to a high column, both included) holds this row's value: a price band, an age group, a fiscal period, a block of IP addresses.

name: join.fuzzy
title: Join on similar text
summary: Bring columns from the other dataset's row whose text is most alike, at or above how alike you ask, with the score of the match: names typed differently, spelling mistakes, words in another order. The same matching the Assistant uses to find duplicates.

name: combine.merge_by_position
title: Put columns side by side
summary: Add the other dataset's columns row by row: its first row beside this one's first, and so on, as pasting columns next to each other does. This dataset keeps its rows; the run says when the other is longer or shorter.

name: combine.intersect
title: Keep rows the other dataset also has
summary: Keep the rows whose values (in every column, or the ones chosen) the other dataset has too (INTERSECT).

name: combine.except
title: Keep rows the other dataset does not have
summary: Keep the rows whose values (in every column, or the ones chosen) the other dataset does not have (EXCEPT).

name: type.to_text
title: To text
summary: Render as text without inventing decimals.

name: type.to_number
title: To number
summary: Read as a number. Values that will not parse become null.

name: type.to_integer
title: To whole number
summary: Read as a whole number, dropping any fraction.

name: type.to_boolean
title: To true/false
summary: Read yes/no/1/0/true/false. Anything else becomes null.

name: type.detect
title: Detect the type
summary: Report what each value looks like, without changing it.

name: type.strip_currency
title: Strip currency symbols
summary: Remove symbols and grouping, leaving text a number parser can read.

name: type.parse_number_locale
title: Parse a localised number
summary: Read a number written with European or US grouping.

name: type.json_path
title: Read a JSON field
summary: Pull one value out of JSON by dotted path. Missing paths become null.

name: type.cast
title: Change the type
summary: Declare a column's type. Values that do not fit become null.

name: type.coerce_with_fallback
title: Convert with a fallback
summary: Read as a number, using a fixed value where it will not parse.

name: date.year
title: Year
summary: Extract the year.

name: date.quarter
title: Quarter
summary: Extract the quarter.

name: date.month
title: Month number
summary: Extract the month number.

name: date.week
title: ISO week
summary: Extract the iso week.

name: date.day
title: Day of month
summary: Extract the day of month.

name: date.day_of_week
title: Day of week
summary: Extract the day of week. Monday is 1, Sunday is 7.

name: date.day_of_year
title: Day of year
summary: Extract the day of year.

name: date.hour
title: Hour
summary: Extract the hour.

name: date.minute
title: Minute
summary: Extract the minute.

name: date.second
title: Second
summary: Extract the second.

name: date.month_name
title: Month name
summary: The month's name.

name: date.day_name
title: Day name
summary: The weekday's name.

name: date.start_of_period
title: Start of period
summary: The first instant of the containing period.

name: date.end_of_period
title: End of period
summary: The last instant of the containing period -- not the start of the next one.

name: date.add_days
title: Add days
summary: Shift by a number of days.

name: date.add_months
title: Add months
summary: Shift by whole months, clamping to the end of a short month.

name: date.add_years
title: Add years
summary: Shift by whole years.

name: date.add_business_days
title: Add business days
summary: Shift by working days, skipping Saturdays and Sundays.

name: date.days_between
title: Days until
summary: Days until another date column, counted from this one.

name: date.months_between
title: Months until
summary: Months until another date column, counted from this one.

name: date.years_between
title: Years until
summary: Years until another date column, counted from this one.

name: date.seconds_between
title: Seconds until
summary: Seconds until another date column, counted from this one.

name: date.business_days_between
title: Business days until
summary: Business days until another date column, counted from this one.

name: date.age_years
title: Age in years
summary: Whole years between this date and today.

name: date.is_weekend
title: Is a weekend
summary: True on Saturday and Sunday.

name: date.fiscal_year
title: Fiscal year
summary: The financial year, named for the calendar year it ends in.

name: date.fiscal_quarter
title: Fiscal quarter
summary: Which quarter of the financial year.

name: date.format
title: Format as text
summary: Render as text with a chosen pattern.

name: date.parse
title: Parse a date
summary: Read text as a date. Values that cannot be read become null.

name: date.to_timestamp
title: Parse a timestamp
summary: Read text as a date and time.

name: date.to_timezone
title: Convert time zone
summary: Move a moment to another time zone. Naive values are read as UTC.

name: date.to_epoch
title: To epoch seconds
summary: Seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC.

name: date.from_epoch
title: From epoch
summary: Read a number of seconds or milliseconds since 1970 as a moment.

name: hash.md5
title: MD5
summary: MD5 digest, in hex. Fast and broken -- fine for change detection, never for secrets.

name: hash.sha1
title: SHA-1
summary: SHA-1 digest, in hex.

name: hash.sha256
title: SHA-256
summary: SHA-256 digest, in hex.

name: hash.sha512
title: SHA-512
summary: SHA-512 digest, in hex.

name: hash.hmac_sha256
title: HMAC SHA-256
summary: Keyed digest, so the same value hashes differently under a different key.

name: privacy.pseudonymise
title: Pseudonymise
summary: A short, stable token per value, salted so it cannot be looked up elsewhere.

name: privacy.mask_partial
title: Mask, keeping the ends
summary: Hide the middle, leaving a few characters visible for recognition.

name: privacy.mask_full
title: Mask completely
summary: Replace every character, keeping the length.

name: encode.base64
title: Base64 encode
summary: Encode as base64.

name: encode.base64_decode
title: Base64 decode
summary: Decode base64. Values that are not valid base64 become null.

name: encode.url
title: URL encode
summary: Percent-encode for use in a URL.

name: encode.url_decode
title: URL decode
summary: Decode percent-encoding.

name: encode.html
title: HTML escape
summary: Escape characters that would otherwise be markup.

name: encode.html_unescape
title: HTML unescape
summary: Turn HTML entities back into characters.

name: code.sql
title: Transform with SQL
summary: Write a SELECT over the data at this step, called input: filters, new columns, groups, joins of input with itself and window functions. It is checked and pushed down like any step, and its columns are known before it runs.

name: code.python
title: Transform with Python
summary: Run Python on the rows, as a pandas DataFrame called data; what it leaves in result (or data) goes on. It runs in the notebook's sandbox, with its limits on memory, time, imports and the network, and is turned off where those limits cannot be held.

name: code.json_query
title: Query JSON (jq)
summary: Take values out of JSON text with a jq-style query: paths (.customer.id), positions (.items[0]), every element (.items[]), pipes, and length, keys, values, first, last, join(", "), map(.name) and tostring. Several answers come back as a JSON list.

name: code.lookup_table
title: Look up in a small table
summary: Replace values from a table written here, value=replacement on each line (codes to names), keeping or emptying what is not listed, or writing a default. Pushes down.

name: code.template
title: Write text from a template
summary: Write a new text column from a template with {column} where each column's value goes (an empty value writes nothing; {{ and }} write braces): an email greeting, a label, a URL.

name: code.http_enrich
title: Look up each value in a web service
summary: Call a web service once for each different value (GET with {value} in the address, or POST a JSON body) and keep part of its JSON answer, picked with a jq-style query. Only hosts an administrator allows; a secret comes from the server's own settings, never the recipe. The run says how many calls it made.

name: geo.geocode
title: Find places from addresses
summary: The latitude and longitude of each address, from the Nominatim-style geocoding service an administrator sets (GEOCODER_URL), one call per different address, at most one a second to OpenStreetMap's own server as it asks.

name: geo.reverse_geocode
title: Find addresses from places
summary: The address (or its city, postcode or country) of each latitude and longitude, from the configured geocoding service.

name: geo.distance
title: Distance between two places
summary: The distance between two latitude and longitude pairs: haversine on a sphere (within about 0.5%, and it runs in the database) or on the WGS84 ellipsoid by Vincenty's method (to the millimetre).

name: geo.bearing
title: Direction to another place
summary: The initial compass bearing, in degrees from north (0 to 360), from one place towards another along the great circle.

name: geo.within_radius
title: Within a distance of a place
summary: True for places within a distance (haversine) of a centre you give: customers within 10 km of a shop.

name: geo.parse_coordinates
title: Read coordinates
summary: Read a place written as text into latitude and longitude columns: "51.5, -0.12", degrees, minutes and seconds such as 51°30'26"N 0°7'39"W, or WKT POINT (lon lat). Anything out of range is empty.

name: geo.make_point
title: Make a point from coordinates
summary: Write a latitude and longitude as one WKT point (POINT (lon lat)) in a geography column.

name: geo.point_in_polygon
title: Inside an area
summary: True for places inside an area you give as WKT or GeoJSON (a delivery zone, a region), by longitude and latitude on the map.

name: geo.region
title: Which region a place is in
summary: Bring columns from the shape (in another dataset of named areas, as WKT or GeoJSON) that contains each place: its country, sales territory, or time zone from a time zone boundary file such as timezone-boundary-builder's.

name: geo.nearest
title: Nearest place in another dataset
summary: Bring columns from the nearest place in another dataset (each customer's nearest store), with the distance to it in kilometres.

name: geo.bounding_box
title: Bounding box of a shape
summary: The smallest box around a shape, as JSON with min_lon, min_lat, max_lon and max_lat.

name: geo.centroid
title: Centre of a shape
summary: The centre of a shape as a WKT point (its centre of mass on the map, which for shapes the size of a country is close to, not exactly, the centre on the globe).

name: geo.area
title: Area of a shape
summary: The area of a polygon on the earth, on a sphere of the earth's mean radius (holes taken away), in square metres, hectares or square kilometres.

name: geo.buffer
title: Grow a shape by a distance
summary: A shape grown outwards by a distance in metres (a circle around a point), measured on a map centred on the shape so the distance holds in every direction.

name: geo.to_geojson
title: Write a shape as GeoJSON
summary: Write a WKT shape as GeoJSON, for a map or an API.

name: geo.geohash_encode
title: Geohash of a place
summary: The geohash of a latitude and longitude: a short code for a cell on the map, longer for a smaller cell (7 characters is about 150 m), shared by places near each other.

name: geo.geohash_decode
title: Place of a geohash
summary: The latitude and longitude of the centre of a geohash's cell.

name: lookup.from_dataset
title: Look up values
summary: Bring columns from the first row of another dataset whose key columns match this row's, or a default; never more rows than before (a VLOOKUP). Look up a key by a value just as well: match on any column.

name: lookup.hierarchy
title: Look up in a hierarchy
summary: From a table of items and their parents (a category tree, an org chart), give each row its path from the top, its level, its top ancestor or its parent.

name: lookup.date_dimension
title: Add calendar columns
summary: Add the year, quarter, month and its name, ISO week, day of the week and its name, day of the year, weekend, fiscal year and quarter (and, given a country, public holidays) for a date: a date dimension without a table to join.

name: lookup.currency_rate
title: Convert at historical rates
summary: Convert an amount using the rate for its currency that was in force on its date, from a table of rates (currency, from date, rate): each row takes the latest rate on or before its date.

name: lookup.company_from_domain
title: Company from a web domain
summary: Bring the company for an email address, a web address or a domain, from a dataset of domains and companies you provide (subdomains find their parent: mail.acme.com is acme.com's).

name: lookup.country_from_ip
title: Country from an IP address
summary: Bring the country (or any column) for an IPv4 or IPv6 address from a dataset of address ranges you provide, such as DB-IP's free country file (start, end, country), whose ranges do not overlap.

name: dedupe.keep_most_complete
title: Keep the most complete of repeats
summary: Of rows that share these columns, keep the one with the fewest empty values (the first of those that tie).

name: dedupe.mark
title: Mark repeats
summary: Add a true or false column that is true on each row repeating an earlier one in these columns, to look at before removing.

name: dedupe.count
title: Count repeats
summary: Add how many rows share each row's values in these columns (1 for a row seen once).

name: dedupe.fuzzy
title: Remove near repeats
summary: Remove rows whose value is alike an earlier row's (spelling mistakes, capitals, Ltd and Limited), keeping the first; the run says how many went.

name: match.cluster
title: Group alike values
summary: Number groups of values that are alike, so rows written differently share a number (empty values have none).

name: match.canonical
title: Replace alike values with one spelling
summary: Write every value of a group of alike values the way most rows write it (the first in order when they tie).

name: match.survivorship
title: Merge repeats into one row
summary: Make one row from each group of rows that share these columns, taking every column's value by a rule: from the most complete row, the most recent, the most common value, the longest, the first or the last (empty values are passed over).

name: match.golden_record
title: Make one record per real thing
summary: Group rows whose column is alike (the same matching as Remove near repeats), then make one row per group by a survivorship rule, numbered so each golden record can be traced.

name: meta.describe_column
title: Describe a column
summary: Say what a column of the output means; each run writes it to the dataset's catalogue entry.

name: meta.tag_column
title: Tag a column
summary: Give a column of the output tags (finance, gdpr, kpi), written to its catalogue entry each run.

name: meta.classify_column
title: Classify a column
summary: Say how sensitive a column of the output is: public, internal, confidential or restricted.

name: meta.mark_personal
title: Mark personal data
summary: Say a column of the output holds personal data, and of what kind, for the catalogue, retention and erasure requests to find; who may see it is set by policies.

name: meta.glossary_term
title: Link a column to a glossary term
summary: Bind a column of the output to a term in the project's glossary (revenue, active customer), so the term knows where its data is.

name: meta.owner
title: Set the dataset's owner
summary: Name the person who answers for the output dataset, by their username; written to its catalogue entry each run.

name: meta.describe_dataset
title: Describe the dataset
summary: Say what the output dataset is for; written to its catalogue entry each run.

name: ml.kmeans
title: Group rows by k-means
summary: Put rows into k clusters of rows alike in the number columns chosen; the run gives the silhouette (how well separated they are).

name: ml.hierarchical
title: Group rows by merging nearest
summary: Build clusters by merging the nearest rows and groups step by step (agglomerative), cut at k clusters.

name: ml.dbscan
title: Group rows by density
summary: Find clusters of any shape as crowded regions (DBSCAN); rows in no crowd are left without a cluster.

name: ml.pca
title: Reduce to principal components
summary: Replace many correlated number columns with a few components that keep most of their variation (PCA); the run says how much each keeps.

name: ml.anomaly_score
title: Score how unusual each row is
summary: A score from 0 (the most ordinary row) to 1 (the most unusual) from an isolation forest over the number columns.

name: ml.forecast_arima
title: Forecast with ARIMA
summary: Forecast the next periods of a series with an ARIMA model of the order given (p,d,q), with an interval from the model.

name: ml.forecast_smoothing
title: Forecast with exponential smoothing
summary: Forecast with Holt-Winters exponential smoothing: a level, a trend and (given its length) a season.

name: ml.forecast_trend_season
title: Forecast a trend and a season
summary: Forecast with a straight-line trend plus a repeating season (sines and cosines of its length), fitted by least squares: the additive model Prophet popularised, without its changepoints.

name: ml.impute_knn
title: Fill gaps from alike rows
summary: Fill an empty number with the average of the rows most alike in the other columns (k nearest neighbours).

name: ml.impute_iterative
title: Fill gaps by regression
summary: Fill empty numbers by predicting each column from the others, round after round until the answers settle (iterative imputation).

name: ml.naive_bayes
title: Predict a label (naive Bayes)
summary: Learn a label from the rows that have it, using number columns, and predict it for every row, with how sure (Gaussian naive Bayes); the run gives the cross-validated accuracy.

name: ml.decision_tree
title: Predict a label (decision tree)
summary: Learn a label from the rows that have it with a decision tree of limited depth, predict it for every row, and say which columns it relies on.

name: ml.feature_importance
title: Which columns matter most
summary: How much each column helps predict another: how much worse a random forest does when that column is shuffled (permutation importance).

name: ml.one_hot
title: One column per value (one-hot)
summary: Turn a column of categories into one 0-or-1 column for each value, for a model that needs numbers.

name: ml.ordinal
title: Number the categories
summary: Give each category a number: in the order you list, or alphabetical (for a model that needs numbers and an order that means something).

name: ml.target_encode
title: Replace categories with their average outcome
summary: Replace each category with the average of a target column for it, pulled towards the overall average when it has few rows (smoothing), for a model that needs numbers.

name: ml.tfidf
title: Key words of each text (TF-IDF)
summary: For each text, the words that set it apart from the rest (term frequency times inverse document frequency), as a JSON object of word to weight.

name: ml.similarity_matrix
title: Most alike rows
summary: For each row, the rows most alike it by cosine similarity: of number columns, or of one text column's words (TF-IDF). Rows are counted from 1.

name: nested.flatten
title: Flatten object into columns
summary: Turn a column holding an object into one column per field, named by their path.

name: nested.explode
title: Explode array into rows
summary: Turn a column holding an array into one row per element, repeating the other columns.

name: nested.json_extract
title: Extract a value by path
summary: Pull one value out of a JSON column by its dotted path, e.g. `address.city` or `items.0.sku`.

name: nested.collect
title: Collect rows into an array
summary: The inverse of explode: gather a column's values into one array per group.

name: nested.infer_json_schema
title: Describe a JSON column's shape
summary: Replace the table with one row per field found in a JSON column: its path, the types seen there, and how many documents actually have it.

name: nested.normalise
title: Split a nested array into its own table
summary: Turn one document with a repeated section into a child table, carrying the parent's key so the two can be joined back together.

name: null.fill_constant
title: Fill blanks with a value
summary: Replace nulls with a fixed value.

name: null.fill_from_column
title: Fill blanks from another column
summary: Where this column is null, take the value from another.

name: null.empty_to_null
title: Treat blanks as missing
summary: Turn empty and whitespace-only text into a real null.

name: null.null_to_empty
title: Treat missing as blank
summary: Turn nulls into empty text, for systems that cannot express null.

name: null.normalise_tokens
title: Recognise 'NA' as missing
summary: Turn the strings exports use for nothing -- NA, N/A, NULL, -, unknown -- into real nulls.

name: null.is_blank
title: Flag blanks
summary: True where the value is missing or only whitespace.

name: numeric.round
title: Round
summary: Round to a number of decimal places.

name: numeric.round_up
title: Round up
summary: Round towards positive infinity.

name: numeric.round_down
title: Round down
summary: Round towards negative infinity.

name: numeric.truncate
title: Truncate
summary: Drop the fractional part, towards zero.

name: numeric.round_to_multiple
title: Round to a multiple
summary: Round to the nearest multiple of a step.

name: numeric.ceil_to_multiple
title: Round a multiple up
summary: Round up to the next multiple of a step.

name: numeric.floor_to_multiple
title: Round a multiple down
summary: Round down to the previous multiple of a step.

name: numeric.absolute
title: Absolute value
summary: Drop the sign.

name: numeric.reciprocal
title: Reciprocal
summary: One divided by the value. Null where the value is zero.

name: numeric.square_root
title: Square root
summary: The square root.

name: numeric.power
title: Raise to a power
summary: Raise to an exponent.

name: numeric.log
title: Logarithm
summary: Logarithm to a chosen base. Null for values at or below zero.

name: numeric.ln
title: Natural logarithm
summary: Logarithm to base e.

name: numeric.exponential
title: Exponential
summary: e raised to the value.

name: numeric.modulo
title: Remainder
summary: The remainder after dividing.

name: numeric.integer_divide
title: Integer divide
summary: Divide and drop the remainder.

name: numeric.clamp
title: Clamp to a range
summary: Pull values below the floor up and values above the ceiling down.

name: numeric.is_even
title: Is even
summary: True for even whole numbers.

name: numeric.is_odd
title: Is odd
summary: True for odd whole numbers.

name: numeric.rescale
title: Rescale to a range
summary: Map a known input range onto a new output range.

name: numeric.percent_of
title: Percent of a total
summary: Express as a percentage of a known total.

name: numeric.bin
title: Group into buckets
summary: Label each value by which fixed-width bucket it falls in.

name: rows.filter
title: Keep or drop matching rows
summary: Keep only the rows a test matches, or drop them.

name: rows.filter_formula
title: Keep rows where a formula holds
summary: Keep, or drop, the rows where a formula is true, such as AND([amount] > 100, [region] = "eu"); a row where it is empty is not kept.

name: rows.keep_top
title: Keep the first rows
summary: Keep the first N rows in the dataset's current order.

name: rows.skip
title: Skip the first rows
summary: Drop the first N rows -- the usual fix for a file with a banner above the data.

name: rows.keep_range
title: Keep a range of rows
summary: Keep N rows starting from a position, counting from zero.

name: rows.sort
title: Sort rows
summary: Order by one or more columns. Where nulls go is stated, not left to the engine.

name: rows.deduplicate
title: Remove duplicate rows
summary: Keep one row per distinct combination -- of every column, or of the ones you name.

name: rows.drop_blank
title: Drop blank rows
summary: Remove rows that are empty -- in every column, or in any of the ones you name.

name: sample.random
title: Random sample
summary: Keep a random share (or number) of the rows, the same ones every run for the same seed.

name: sample.stratified
title: Sample each group alike
summary: Keep the same share (or number) of rows from every group, so small groups are not lost from the sample.

name: sample.systematic
title: Every nth row
summary: Keep every nth row, starting from a given row.

name: sample.cluster
title: Sample whole groups
summary: Choose some groups at random and keep all their rows (cluster sampling: a few shops, every sale in each).

name: sample.reservoir
title: Sample a fixed number in one pass
summary: Keep exactly this many rows, each row as likely as any other, in one pass over the data (reservoir sampling, for when the total is not known first).

name: sample.balanced
title: Balance the groups
summary: Keep the same number of rows of every value of a column, as many as the smallest group has (for a model that would otherwise learn the commonest answer).

name: sample.train_test
title: Split into training and test rows
summary: Label each row train or test at random, a share in test, optionally the same share within each value of a column (stratified).

name: sample.time_split
title: Split by time
summary: Label rows after a date (or the latest share of them) test and the rest train, so a model is judged on data from after what it learnt from.

name: sample.split_by_condition
title: Label rows by a condition
summary: Label each row by whether a formula holds for it, with words of your choosing (big and small orders), to filter or deliver each part separately.

name: sample.split_into_parts
title: Number the rows into parts
summary: Number each row 1 to N to split the data into N parts: in order (the first rows are part 1) or in turn (1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3).

name: stats.describe
title: Describe the columns
summary: One row per column: how many values and empty ones, how many different, and for numbers the mean, spread, lowest, quartiles, median and highest; the commonest value for every column.

name: stats.correlation_matrix
title: Correlation matrix
summary: How closely every pair of number columns moves together, from -1 to 1, by Pearson (straight-line), Spearman (rank) or Kendall's tau.

name: stats.covariance_matrix
title: Covariance matrix
summary: The covariance of every pair of number columns (sample, n - 1).

name: stats.histogram
title: Histogram
summary: Count the values in equal-width bins between the lowest and highest (the last bin includes the highest).

name: stats.frequency
title: Frequency table
summary: How often each value appears, commonest first, with its share and the running share.

name: stats.outliers_iqr
title: Find outliers by the middle half
summary: True for values more than 1.5 times the interquartile range below the lower quartile or above the upper (Tukey's fences).

name: stats.outliers_zscore
title: Find outliers by standard deviations
summary: True for values more than 3 standard deviations from the mean (suits values that are roughly normal).

name: stats.outliers_mad
title: Find outliers by median deviation
summary: True for values whose modified z-score, from the median absolute deviation, is above 3.5 (robust to the outliers themselves).

name: stats.outliers_isolation_forest
title: Find unusual rows
summary: True for rows that an isolation forest separates from the rest quickly, looking at several number columns at once; a score says how unusual each is.

name: stats.normality
title: Test for a normal distribution
summary: Test whether the values could come from a normal distribution: Shapiro-Wilk, or D'Agostino-Pearson past 5,000 values.

name: stats.t_test
title: Compare means (t-test)
summary: Test whether the mean differs from a value (one-sample), or between two groups (Welch's two-sample, not assuming equal spreads).

name: stats.paired_t_test
title: Compare before and after (paired t-test)
summary: Test whether two columns measured on the same rows (before and after) differ on average.

name: stats.anova
title: Compare means of several groups (ANOVA)
summary: Test whether the mean is the same in every group (one-way analysis of variance).

name: stats.chi_square
title: Test whether two categories are related (chi-square)
summary: Test whether two columns of categories are independent, or one tells you something about the other.

name: stats.mann_whitney
title: Compare two groups without assuming normal (Mann-Whitney)
summary: Test whether values in one group tend to be larger than in the other, by ranks.

name: stats.ks_test
title: Compare distributions (Kolmogorov-Smirnov)
summary: Test whether two groups are distributed alike, or one column like a normal distribution with its own mean and spread.

name: stats.linear_regression
title: Fit a straight line
summary: How one number column moves with another: the intercept and slope by least squares, their standard errors and p-values, and R².

name: stats.multiple_regression
title: Fit several columns at once
summary: How one number column moves with several others together (ordinary least squares), with each one's estimate, standard error and p-value.

name: stats.logistic_regression
title: Fit a yes-or-no outcome
summary: How several columns change the odds of a 0-or-1 outcome (logistic regression by maximum likelihood), with each one's estimate and p-value.

name: stats.residuals
title: Add fitted values and residuals
summary: Fit the column by least squares on others and add, on every row, the fitted value and the residual (what the fit misses), to look for what it does not explain.

name: stats.confidence_interval
title: Confidence interval for the mean
summary: The range the true mean is likely in, by Student's t, overall or for each group.

name: stats.sample_size
title: How many to sample
summary: How many responses a survey needs for a margin of error at a confidence, for a share near the one expected (0.5 when unknown), optionally in a finite population. Uses no data.

name: stats.seasonal_decompose
title: Split into trend and season
summary: Separate a series, in time order, into its trend (a centred moving average), its repeating seasonal pattern of the period given, and what is left (classical decomposition, additive or multiplicative).

name: stats.autocorrelation
title: Autocorrelation by lag
summary: How much a series, in time order, resembles itself this many rows earlier, for each lag, with the 95% band chance alone stays inside.

name: stats.trend_test
title: Test for a trend
summary: Is a series, in time order, rising or falling beyond chance? The Mann-Kendall test, with Sen's slope for how fast.

name: stats.changepoints
title: Find where the level changes
summary: Number the stretches of a series, in time order, between points where its average shifts (binary segmentation with a penalty so noise does not count), 1 for the first stretch.

name: stats.distribution_fit
title: Fit a distribution
summary: Which of the normal, uniform, exponential and (for positive values) lognormal, gamma and Weibull distributions describes the values best, by maximum likelihood, ranked by AIC, each with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov check.

name: columns.add
title: Add a column with one value
summary: Add a column holding the same value on every row: a source label, a default, a flag to fill in later.

name: columns.split_by_position
title: Split at fixed positions
summary: Cut text into pieces after given numbers of characters (fixed-width records, codes with parts).

name: columns.split_by_pattern
title: Split by a pattern
summary: Split text into columns wherever a regular expression matches: any run of spaces, a dash or a slash, a comma with or without a space.

name: columns.split_to_rows
title: Split into rows
summary: Give each value in a list ("red, green, blue") its own row, repeating the other columns.

name: columns.promote_headers
title: Use the first row as column names
summary: Take the column names from the first row and drop it, for a file whose header was read as data. A blank name becomes column_N.

name: columns.demote_headers
title: Turn column names into the first row
summary: Move the column names into a first row and name the columns column_1, column_2: for data that has to be read without a header.

name: rows.keep_last
title: Keep the last rows
summary: Keep this many rows from the end, in their order.

name: rows.skip_last
title: Skip the last rows
summary: Drop this many rows from the end (a totals line, a footer).

name: rows.reverse
title: Reverse the rows
summary: Put the rows in the opposite order.

name: rows.shuffle
title: Shuffle the rows
summary: Put the rows in a random order that is the same every run for the same seed.

name: rows.delete
title: Delete rows by number
summary: Delete the rows at these positions, counted from 1 in the order the rows are in.

name: rows.insert
title: Add a row
summary: Add one row with the values given, at the start or the end; columns not named are empty.

name: rows.custom_order
title: Sort in a chosen order
summary: Put rows in the order of a list of values (Low, Medium, High; Mon to Sun); values not in the list come after.

name: rows.keep_errors
title: Keep rows that do not convert
summary: Keep only the rows whose value cannot be read as a number, a date or true or false, to see what is wrong.

name: rows.remove_errors
title: Drop rows that do not convert
summary: Drop the rows whose value cannot be read as a number, a date or true or false; empty values stay.

name: reshape.transpose
title: Swap rows and columns
summary: Turn each column into a row and each row into a column, naming the new columns from a column of your choice (or row_1, row_2).

name: reshape.nest
title: Combine columns into one
summary: Put several columns into one JSON column, for an API that wants an object or a document store.

name: reshape.crosstab
title: Cross-tab two columns
summary: Count (or total) rows by two columns at once: one row per value of the first, one column per value of the second.

name: text.trim
title: Trim whitespace
summary: Remove spaces, tabs and newlines from both ends.

name: text.trim_start
title: Trim leading whitespace
summary: Remove whitespace from the start only.

name: text.trim_end
title: Trim trailing whitespace
summary: Remove whitespace from the end only.

name: text.collapse_whitespace
title: Collapse whitespace
summary: Replace every run of whitespace with a single space, and trim the ends.

name: text.upper
title: UPPERCASE
summary: Convert to upper case.

name: text.lower
title: Lowercase
summary: Convert to lower case.

name: text.title_case
title: Title Case
summary: Capitalise the first letter of every word.

name: text.sentence_case
title: Sentence case
summary: Capitalise the first letter and lower the rest.

name: text.swap_case
title: Swap case
summary: Turn upper case into lower and lower into upper.

name: text.pad_left
title: Pad left
summary: Pad to a fixed width by adding characters on the left.

name: text.pad_right
title: Pad right
summary: Pad to a fixed width by adding characters on the right.

name: text.truncate
title: Truncate
summary: Shorten to a maximum length, optionally ending with a suffix.

name: text.left
title: First characters
summary: Keep the first N characters.

name: text.right
title: Last characters
summary: Keep the last N characters.

name: text.substring
title: Substring
summary: Take a run of characters from a starting position. Positions count from 1.

name: text.extract_before
title: Extract before
summary: Everything before the first occurrence of a marker.

name: text.extract_after
title: Extract after
summary: Everything after the first occurrence of a marker.

name: text.extract_between
title: Extract between
summary: The text between two markers. Null when either marker is missing.

name: text.split_part
title: Take one part
summary: Split on a delimiter and keep one part. Parts count from 1.

name: text.char_at
title: Character at position
summary: The single character at a position, counting from 1.

name: text.regex_extract
title: Extract with a pattern
summary: The first capture group of a regular expression.

name: text.regex_replace
title: Replace with a pattern
summary: Replace everything matching a regular expression.

name: text.regex_count
title: Count pattern matches
summary: How many times a regular expression matches.

name: text.replace
title: Find and replace
summary: Replace every occurrence of one piece of text with another.

name: text.position
title: Position of text
summary: Where a piece of text first appears, counting from 1. Zero when absent.

name: text.count_occurrences
title: Count occurrences
summary: How many times a piece of text appears.

name: text.remove_characters
title: Remove characters
summary: Delete every character in a set.

name: text.keep_characters
title: Keep only characters
summary: Delete everything except the characters in a set.

name: text.translate
title: Swap characters
summary: Replace characters one for one, like tr.

name: text.length
title: Length
summary: How many characters.

name: text.word_count
title: Word count
summary: How many whitespace-separated words.

name: text.reverse
title: Reverse
summary: Reverse the characters.

name: text.repeat
title: Repeat
summary: Repeat the text N times.

name: text.camel_to_words
title: Split camelCase
summary: Insert spaces at camel-case boundaries.

name: text.slugify
title: Make a slug
summary: Lower case, accents folded, everything else turned into hyphens.

name: text.remove_accents
title: Remove accents
summary: Fold accented letters to their plain equivalents.

name: text.strip_html
title: Strip HTML
summary: Remove tags and decode entities, leaving the text.

name: text.normalise_unicode
title: Normalise Unicode
summary: Apply a Unicode normalisation form so equal-looking text compares equal.

name: text.soundex
title: Soundex code
summary: A four-character phonetic code, for matching names that sound alike.

name: text.starts_with
title: Starts with
summary: True when the text begins with a given prefix.

name: text.ends_with
title: Ends with
summary: True when the text ends with a given suffix.

name: text.contains
title: Contains
summary: True when the text contains a given piece.

name: text.merge_columns
title: Merge columns
summary: Join this column to others with a separator, skipping the empty ones.

name: check.is_email
title: Looks like an email
summary: True for text shaped like an email address.

name: check.is_url
title: Looks like a URL
summary: True for text shaped like an http or https URL.

name: check.is_date
title: Reads as a date
summary: True where the value can be read as a date.

name: check.is_number
title: Reads as a number
summary: True where the value can be read as a number.

name: check.in_range
title: Within a range
summary: True where a number falls between two bounds, inclusive.

name: check.matches_pattern
title: Matches a pattern
summary: True where a regular expression matches.

name: check.length_between
title: Length within bounds
summary: True where the text's length falls between two bounds.

name: check.in_set
title: One of a list
summary: True where the value is one of an allowed list.

name: check.quarantine
title: Split on a check column
summary: Keep only the rows that passed a check, or only the ones that failed.

name: text.transliterate
title: Write in Latin letters
summary: Write Cyrillic and Greek in Latin letters and drop accents (Москва to Moskva, Αθήνα to Athina, Øresund to Oresund), for matching and for systems that take plain letters only.

name: text.detect_language
title: Detect the language
summary: Say which language text is written in, as a two-letter code: by its alphabet where that settles it, otherwise by which of 17 languages' commonest words it uses. Texts under three words are not guessed; with confidence on, a second column says how sure (0 to 1).

name: numeric.negate
title: Flip the sign
summary: Turn positive into negative and back (credits into debits).

name: numeric.ratio
title: Divide by another column
summary: This column divided by another, row by row (empty where the other is 0 or empty): a conversion rate, a share, a margin.

name: numeric.convert_currency
title: Convert at a fixed rate
summary: Multiply by an exchange rate you give (for a rate that changes by day, join to a table of rates with Join to the nearest earlier row).

name: numeric.convert_units
title: Convert units
summary: Convert between units of length, mass, volume, area, speed, time, data, energy, pressure and temperature (kilometres to miles, °F to °C, MiB to GB).

name: numeric.bin_custom
title: Group into chosen ranges
summary: Label each value by the range it falls in, from edges you choose (0, 18, 65, 120 gives 0 to 18, 18 to 65, 65 to 120), with your own labels if you like. A value outside every range is empty.

name: numeric.robust_scale
title: Scale by the median and spread
summary: Subtract the median and divide by the spread of the middle half (the interquartile range), so outliers do not stretch the scale.

name: numeric.bin_equal_frequency
title: Group into equal-size groups
summary: Split the values into this many groups holding about the same number of rows each, labelled by the range each covers.

name: type.to_decimal
title: Change to an exact decimal
summary: Read as a number with this many decimal places, kept exact rather than as a float and rounded half up from the value as written (1.005 is 1.01): money, quantities that must add up.

name: type.to_json
title: Write as JSON
summary: Write each value as JSON text: text quoted, numbers as numbers, JSON already there kept as it is.

name: type.to_list
title: Split into a list
summary: Turn text like "red, green" into a JSON list (["red", "green"]), to explode or count later.

name: type.strip_thousands
title: Remove thousands separators
summary: Read numbers written with thousands separators (1,234,567 or 1.234.567,89) as numbers.

name: null.interpolate_linear
title: Fill gaps along a straight line
summary: Fill an empty value between two known ones by drawing a straight line between them, spaced by a date or number column. Gaps before the first or after the last known value stay empty.

name: null.interpolate_spline
title: Fill gaps along a smooth curve
summary: Fill an empty value between known ones with a smooth curve through them (a cubic spline), needing at least three known values.

name: null.drop_mostly_empty
title: Drop mostly empty columns
summary: Drop every column whose share of empty values is above this (0.5 drops columns more than half empty). The first column stays if every one would go.

name: clean.address
title: Standardise an address
summary: Tidy spacing and capitals and write street words one way: in full (Street, Road) or abbreviated (St, Rd), as UK and US addresses use them.

name: clean.address_part
title: Take part of an address
summary: Take the house number, street, unit, city, region, postcode or country from an address written on one line with commas, by UK and US rules (a UK postcode, a US state and ZIP code). A part it cannot find is empty; other countries' addresses mostly give the street and city only.

name: clean.currency_code
title: Standardise a currency
summary: Write a currency as its ISO 4217 code from a symbol or a name (£ or pounds to GBP, € to EUR); 33 currencies.

name: clean.person_name
title: Standardise a person's name
summary: Write a name with the capitals people expect (McDonald, O'Brien, Smith-Jones, Ludwig van Beethoven), tidy spaces, and optionally drop titles such as Mr and Dr.

name: clean.fix_swapped
title: Fix values in the wrong column
summary: Swap two columns' values on the rows where this one does not look like what it should hold and the other does (a phone number typed in the name box). The run says how many rows it swapped.

name: clean.units
title: Standardise measurements
summary: Read measurements written with their units ("5 kg", "5000g", "11 lbs") as numbers in one unit; a value without a unit, or in another kind of unit, is empty.

name: privacy.tokenise
title: Replace with a reversible token
summary: Replace each value with a token that stays the same for the same value (so it still joins and groups) and that only an administrator can turn back, in Administration, each time recorded in the audit log.

name: key.surrogate
title: Make a key from columns
summary: Make one short key from several columns that is the same whenever they are (a hash of the values): a key for a table that has none.

name: key.uuid
title: Make an ID for each row
summary: Give each row a UUID: made from columns you choose (the same values always give the same ID), or random but the same every run for the same seed.

name: window.row_number
title: Row number
summary: Number the rows 1, 2, 3 within each group, in order.

name: window.rank
title: Rank
summary: Rank rows by this column, with ties sharing a rank and the next rank skipped (1, 2, 2, 4).

name: window.dense_rank
title: Dense rank
summary: Rank rows by this column with no gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 3).

name: window.percent_rank
title: Percent rank
summary: Where a row sits in its group, from 0 (first) to 1 (last).

name: window.cume_dist
title: Cumulative distribution
summary: The share of the group's rows at or before this one, from just above 0 to 1.

name: window.ntile
title: Split into equal groups
summary: Number the rows 1 to N in order, so each number has as near an equal share of the rows as possible (quartiles, deciles).

name: window.lag
title: Value from an earlier row
summary: The value this many rows before, within the group (empty before the first).

name: window.lead
title: Value from a later row
summary: The value this many rows after, within the group (empty after the last).

name: window.first_value
title: First value in the group
summary: The group's first value, in order, on every row.

name: window.last_value
title: Last value in the group
summary: The group's last value, in order, on every row.

name: window.nth_value
title: Nth value in the group
summary: The group's value at this position, in order, on every row (empty when the group is shorter).

name: window.cumulative_sum
title: Running total
summary: Add each row's value to the total so far, within the group.

name: window.cumulative_product
title: Running product
summary: Multiply each row's value into the product so far.

name: window.cumulative_max
title: Running highest
summary: The highest value so far, within the group.

name: window.cumulative_min
title: Running lowest
summary: The lowest value so far, within the group.

name: window.cumulative_count
title: Running count
summary: How many values so far, within the group.

name: window.running_average
title: Running average
summary: The average of the values so far, within the group.

name: window.moving_average
title: Moving average
summary: The average of this row and the rows just before it.

name: window.moving_sum
title: Moving total
summary: The total of this row and the rows just before it.

name: window.moving_max
title: Moving highest
summary: The highest of this row and the rows just before it.

name: window.moving_min
title: Moving lowest
summary: The lowest of this row and the rows just before it.

name: window.rolling_stdev
title: Moving standard deviation
summary: How spread out this row and the rows just before it are (empty with only one value).

name: window.ema
title: Exponential moving average
summary: A moving average that weighs recent rows more; the span sets how quickly older rows fade.

name: window.rolling_correlation
title: Moving correlation
summary: How closely this column moves with another over the last rows: 1 together, -1 opposite, 0 unrelated.

name: window.session
title: Number the sessions
summary: Group events into sessions: a new session starts after a gap longer than this many minutes, counted 1, 2, 3 within each group.

name: window.difference
title: Difference from the row before
summary: This row's value minus the one before it in the group (empty for the first).

name: window.percent_change
title: Percent change from the row before
summary: How much this row's value changed from the one before, as a share of it (0.5 is half as much again).

name: window.percent_of_total
title: Percent of the group's total
summary: This row's value as a percentage of its group's total.

name: window.normalise
title: Scale from 0 to 1
summary: Rescale so the group's lowest value is 0 and its highest 1 (empty when every value is the same).

name: window.z_score
title: Standard score
summary: How many standard deviations a value is from its group's average (a z-score).

name: window.top_n_per_group
title: Keep the top rows of each group
summary: Keep the rows with the highest (or lowest) values of a column within each group.

name: null.fill_forward
title: Fill down
summary: Fill an empty value with the last value above it in the group (merged cells, sparse readings).

name: null.fill_backward
title: Fill up
summary: Fill an empty value with the next value below it in the group.
